cross_cutting_observations.title: FR-G1 import ban: ZERO VIOLATIONS across entire module
cross_cutting_observations.description: Exhaustive scan of all 23 files in src/superclaude/cli/eval/ confirms NO imports from superclaude.core, superclaude.agents, superclaude.skills, or any other upstream framework module. The eval/ module is a properly isolated leaf that depends only on: (1) stdlib, (2) third-party packages (click, yaml, jsonschema), (3) internal eval/ modules. References to sprint.executor and prd.executor exist as documentation only, not imports.

cross_cutting_observations.title: Dependency arrows follow expected layering with zero back-edges
cross_cutting_observations.description: The module follows the prescribed layering: commands.py → orchestrator/runner/loader; runner.py → claude_process/pty_driver/expect/isolation/hook_adapter/coverage; reporter/run_report → models/artifact_layout (pure functions); models/config are leaves. No back-edges detected (e.g., models.py does NOT import from runner.py). The TYPE_CHECKING guard in models.py:45-46 correctly isolates the HomeIsolation import for type hints only, preventing runtime circular dependency.
evidence: commands.py:44-96 imports from artifact_layout, capabilities, config, coverage, disk_budget, isolation, loader, models, orchestrator, reporter, runner, signal_handler
runner.py:51-62 imports from config, hook_adapter, isolation, models, retry, signal_handler
models.py:45-46: if TYPE_CHECKING: from .isolation import HomeIsolation
models.py has no non-TYPE_CHECKING imports from runner or any higher layer
config.py and artifact_layout.py are pure leaves (stdlib only)

cross_cutting_observations.title: commands.py (1951L) is borderline god-object; runner.py (1238L), models.py (938L) are justified
cross_cutting_observations.description: commands.py at 1951 lines is the largest file and risks becoming a junk drawer. However, inspection reveals it contains 4 distinct Click command functions (eval_doctor, eval_list, eval_describe, eval_run) plus 11 helpers explicitly scoped to T04.10 (lines 1293-1539). The size is justified by CLI surface area, but the 11 helpers should be monitored for potential extraction. runner.py (1238L) implements a single coherent responsibility (FR-LC1 lifecycle skeleton). models.py (938L) defines 11 dataclasses (EvalSpec, EvalResult, ExpectResult, ExpectFailure, EvalContext, EvalOutcome, RunCounts, RunTotals, RunSummary, EvalResult, plus field ordering tuples) - size is proportional to schema complexity. expect.py (723L), isolation.py (697L), loader.py (624L) are all single-responsibility modules with size justified by comprehensive docstrings and edge-case handling.
recommendations: commands.py: Consider extracting the 11 T04.10 helpers (_utc_iso_now, _new_run_id, _default_output_dir, _can_install_signal_handler, _resolve_executor_factory, _run_one_spec, _compute_run_stats, _format_run_summary_line) into a commands_helpers.py module if the file grows beyond 2000 lines
Monitor commands.py for additional helper accumulation; maintain the 'helpers are module-level for testability' discipline
No immediate action required for runner.py, models.py, or other large files - their size is proportional to their single responsibility

cross_cutting_observations.title: FR-G4 artifact layout: clean boundary between artifact_layout.py and run_report.py
cross_cutting_observations.description: artifact_layout.py (306L) is the single source of truth for path construction (compose_run_dir, compose_run_id, allocate_per_eval_paths, PerEvalPaths dataclass). run_report.py (380L) is the single source of truth for report rendering (render_summary_markdown, render_summary_json, render_junit_xml, write_aggregated_report). The boundary is clean: artifact_layout constructs paths, run_report writes files. No duplication of path structure knowledge across the two modules. reporter.py (234L) is a thin class wrapper over run_report functions.
evidence: artifact_layout.py:allocate_per_eval_paths returns PerEvalPaths with eval_dir, logs_jsonl, tty_transcript, artifacts_dir
run_report.py:write_aggregated_report(summary, output_dir) writes summary.md, summary.json, junit.xml under output_dir
No path construction logic in run_report.py; no file writing logic in artifact_layout.py

cross_cutting_observations.title: No overlapping data types across config.py, models.py, capabilities.py
cross_cutting_observations.description: config.py defines EvalConfig (frozen config dataclass with paths, defaults, allowed_scratch_roots). models.py defines 11 manifest/runtime dataclasses (EvalSpec, EvalResult, ExpectResult, etc.). capabilities.py defines Capability, CapabilityGates, CapabilityReport, CapabilityStatus. No overlap detected - each module owns a distinct domain. EvalConfig is pre-run configuration; models.py types are runtime/post-run data; capabilities.py types are pre-run gates. No data duplication across the three.
evidence: config.py:EvalConfig has fields: paths (Mapping), defaults (Mapping), allowed_scratch_roots (tuple[Path]), min_claude_version (tuple[int])
models.py types: EvalSpec (manifest entry), EvalResult/ExpectResult (runtime), RunSummary/RunCounts/RunTotals (aggregated post-run)
capabilities.py types: Capability (gate definition), CapabilityGates (gate enforcement), CapabilityReport (gate result)
No field name overlap, no semantic duplication

cross_cutting_observations.title: Helper _new_run_id in commands.py could be co-located with compose_run_id in artifact_layout.py
cross_cutting_observations.description: commands.py:1322 defines _new_run_id as a thin wrapper over artifact_layout.compose_run_id. The docstring (lines 1325-1331) explicitly justifies keeping it in commands.py for symbol-contract reasons (tests assert _new_run_id is importable from commands). However, this creates two entry points for the same functionality. The other 10 helpers (_utc_iso_now, _default_output_dir, _can_install_signal_handler, _resolve_executor_factory, _run_one_spec, _compute_run_stats, _format_run_summary_line, _NullLifecycleExecutor class, plus 2 more) are correctly scoped to commands.py as they are CLI-specific. Only _new_run_id is a candidate for co-location with the artifact_layout module it wraps.
cross_cutting_observations.recommendation: Consider: (1) Keep current structure (justified by test contract), or (2) Move _new_run_id into artifact_layout.py and update tests to import from there. Current structure is defensible but creates a minor indirection.
evidence: artifact_layout.py:139: compose_run_id is the canonical implementation
Test contract: tests/cli/eval/test_single_command.py asserts _new_run_id importable from commands

cross_cutting_observations.title: eval_run is well-decomposed via 11 helpers; no god-function anti-pattern
cross_cutting_observations.description: eval_run (commands.py:1644-1950, ~306 lines) is decomposed via 11 module-level helpers added in commit e6368db8. The function body is a linear pipeline: flag validation → output-dir resolution → suite loading → capability gating → coverage gating → orchestrator wiring → signal handling → outcome tallying → reporter writing → exit-code determination. Each step delegates to a focused helper. The 11 helpers (lines 1293-1539) are testable in isolation and maintain the single-responsibility principle. No 200+-line god-function detected.
evidence: eval_run body: delegates to helpers at every step, ~306L total

cross_cutting_observations.title: Single source of truth: config.py owns ALL config loading
cross_cutting_observations.description: config.py defines EvalConfig and resolve_scratch_root. No other files in src/superclaude/cli/eval/ load YAML/JSON configuration independently. Suite manifests are loaded by loader.py:validate_manifest, which returns ParsedSuite objects fed into SuiteLoader. Settings.json (for hook matchers) is loaded by coverage.py:extract_hook_matchers, which is a pure parser - not a config loader. All runtime configuration flows through EvalConfig. Single source of truth confirmed.
evidence: config.py:84-105: EvalConfig dataclass (paths, defaults, allowed_scratch_roots, min_claude_version)
loader.py:validate_manifest reads YAML but returns EvalSpec list, not config
coverage.py:extract_hook_matchers reads settings.json for matcher patterns, not config
No other file in eval/ defines config-loading functions

cross_cutting_observations.title: Exit-code constants: single source of truth per constant, consistent references
cross_cutting_observations.description: RUN_CLEAN_EXIT_CODE (=0), RUN_FAILURES_EXIT_CODE (=1), RUN_INTERRUPTED_EXIT_CODE (=3) are defined once in commands.py:570-577. RUN_INTERRUPTED_EXIT_CODE re-exports signal_handler.EXIT_INTERRUPTED to maintain single source of truth. No magic number duplicates detected. Other exit-code constants follow the same pattern: SCHEMA_ERROR_EXIT_CODE, INVALID_EVAL_ID_EXIT_CODE, UNRESOLVED_CAPABILITY_EXIT_CODE, SUITE_LOADER_ERROR_EXIT_CODE all =2 per design-spec §4 (harness error), defined once in their respective modules (loader.py, config.py, coverage.py, disk_budget.py, run_report.py). All exit-code constants are exported in __init__.py. Usage sites reference constants, not literals.
evidence: No magic number literals (0, 1, 2, 3) used directly in sys.exit calls

cross_cutting_observations.title: Schema-vs-model alignment: schemas/summary.schema.json and suites/suite.schema.json align with models.py
cross_cutting_observations.description: schemas/summary.schema.json (254L) defines runCounts (manifest_n, expanded_n_prime, kept_k, skipped_s, kept_plus_skipped_equals_n_prime), runTotals (passed, failed, skipped, errored, interrupted, timeout), evalOutcome (eval_id, title, status, duration_sec, expects, skip_reason, skip_flag_triggered, artifacts, error_class), expectResult (name, passed, message, details, duration_sec, failure), expectFailure (eval_id, expect_id, expect_name, expected, actual, message, artifact_ref, traceback). These match models.py dataclasses verbatim. suites/suite.schema.json (162L) defines evalEntry shape matching EvalSpec (id, title, category, requires, timeout_sec, isolation, inputs, expects, parameterize, no_pty). Field names and types align. Comments in both schemas explicitly reference the corresponding models.py dataclasses as source of truth. No drift detected.
evidence: summary.schema.json:148: DM-001 EvalOutcome serialised by EvalOutcome.to_dict()
summary.schema.json:203: DM-009 ExpectResult serialised by ExpectResult.to_dict()
summary.schema.json:228: DM-005 ExpectFailure serialised by ExpectFailure.to_dict()
models.py:720-738: RunCounts dataclass fields match summary.schema.json:runCounts
models.py:740-781: RunTotals dataclass fields match summary.schema.json:runTotals
models.py:66-98: EvalSpec dataclass fields match suite.schema.json:evalEntry

summary.god_object_status: WARNING - commands.py at 1951L is borderline; monitor for helper extraction
summary.missing_abstraction_status: MINOR - _new_run_id wrapper is a minor indirection
summary.exit_code_constants_status: PASS - single source of truth, consistent references
summary.overall_assessment: The cliEval module exhibits strong architectural discipline. The FR-G1 import ban is perfectly enforced (zero violations), layering is correct with no back-edges, exit-code constants are properly centralized, and schemas align with models. The only architectural concern is commands.py approaching 2000 lines, but the size is justified by 4 CLI commands + 11 well-factored helpers. The module is production-ready from an architecture perspective.
